title: Silvergate Bank - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
summary: Discovery with Silvergate Bank focused on whether Redwood Hosted can meet data residency and logging constraints vs Dedicated/Private deployments. Customer emphasized strict audit/logging retention limits, in-region data residency for EU customers, and KMS control. Team agreed to share SOC2/HIPAA docs, dedicated pricing, and schedule a technical deep dive.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15
Time: 14:00 - 14:47 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Leah Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jennifer Park (CISO, Silvergate), Aaron Miles (Cloud Architect), Sonia Patel (Head of AI), Tom Reyes (VP Ops)

[00:00] Leah: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. quick roll call?
[00:10] Jennifer: jen park here, ciso.
[00:12] Aaron: aaron, cloud arch.
[00:15] Sonia: sonia, head of ai.
[00:18] Tom: tom here.
[00:20] Marco: marco from redwood, se.
[00:22] Leah: great. goal for today: dig into data residency, logging, and what deployment model makes sense for you (hosted, dedicated, private). we'll capture constraints and next steps.

[01:02] Jennifer: to be blunt, we have pretty strict requirements. for our EU retail customers data must be stored and processed in eu for GDPR. also for certain products we have to meet bank regulatory audit requirements — logs, retention windows, and ability to redact.
[01:27] Leah: understood. is the EU residency requirement per-customer or per-product?
[01:33] Sonia: per-product; our consumer payments product must keep all tokens and metadata in eu. other internal analytics can live us-east.

[02:05] Marco: about deployment options, quick primer: Hosted means our managed control plane and storage; we can offer region-specific hosting (e.g., eu-west1) but keys are managed by redwood by default. Dedicated is reserved capacity in a tenancy we control for you that can be limited to a region, and Private gives you VPC + customer-managed KMS or on-prem. each step increases customer control and isolation.
[02:38] Aaron: what's the default key management in hosted? we need to know if redwood holds keys — that won't fly for some workloads.
[02:45] Leah: default is redwood-managed KMS. we do support customer-managed keys (CMK) for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we can do bring-your-own-key in some enterprise agreements, but typically CMK is standard in Private. we can document options.

[03:20] Jennifer: also, audit logs — regulators want immutable logs for API access and for the model outputs in case of disputes. we can't have logs that contain raw pii or full customer messages in plain text unless we control retention.
[03:38] Priya: quick note — we support log redaction and tokenization pipelines. for private deployments you can choose log forwarding to your SIEM and set retention policies. hosted can limit retention and mask certain fields, but retention controls are more limited unless we do a dedicated contract.

[04:10] Tom: do you offer SOC2 + HIPAA attestation? we've got a few pilots that will touch phi.
[04:18] Leah: yes we are SOC 2 type 2 and we maintain HIPAA BAAs for qualified customers. i'll send the pack after this call.

[04:45] Sonia: on the inference side, we need to know whether KV cache and prefix caching could accidentally persist sensitive identifiers. is there a way to ensure ephemeral caching or to disable kv cache persistence?
[05:02] Marco: great question. our runtime keeps KV cache in memory for inference speed; on Hosted it's ephemeral per instance and not written to disk. for Private you can enforce never-write-to-disk and put strict TTLs, and we have a setting to completely disable cache persistence. i'll add config details in the topology doc.

[05:38] Leah: can you talk about throughput and latency expectations? you mentioned pilot QPS?
[05:45] Aaron: pilot will be low (10–20 qps) but production could be 200–300 qps for certain flows. latency target is sub-200ms p50 for short prompts; longer context is fine but we need predictable tails.

[06:10] Marco: Dedicated gives predictable GPU pools and isolation, which helps with tail latency. Hosted uses shared pools and smart routing; for most customers it's fine but high-volume low-latency apps often pick Dedicated.

[06:35] Jennifer: GDPR concern: if we have hosted in eu but support engineers at redwood in us, is that a cross-border transfer risk? we need guarantees about who can access logs and data.
[06:51] Leah: good point. we can restrict admin access by region on Dedicated/Private and enforce SSO roles. for Hosted we have controls but some support access still routes through us. we can include a controls matrix in the packet.

[07:20] Sonia: another thing — do you store model outputs or do you treat them as transient? for compliance we sometimes must store the output in our systems, but we don't want the provider to store it in a way that would cause data exfil risk.
[07:35] Marco: by default we store short-term logs for monitoring and can disable storage of full outputs; you can configure redaction at the application layer and suppress storing the output. Private gives you the strongest guarantee — no persisted outputs on redwood-managed storage unless you opt in.

[08:05] Aaron: networking — can we do VPC peering or private link to avoid public endpoints?
[08:12] Priya: yes, Private supports VPC peering and private endpoints. Dedicated can be set up in your cloud account with private networking. Hosted uses internet endpoints, but we provide IP allow lists and mTLS if needed.

[08:45] Jennifer: logs retention: regulators want 7 years for certain logs, but security team wants to keep PII removed after 90 days. can you do tiered retention?
[09:00] Leah: we support tiered retention in Dedicated/Private; Hosted can do configurable retention windows but long-term archiving is limited unless we set up custom storage. we'll note specifics in the doc.

[09:30] Marco: i want to call out an operational tradeoff — long retention for full request/response can increase cost and blow up token storage; many customers instead store a hashed pointer and the minimal metadata. we can help design a redaction/hashing scheme.

[10:05] Sonia: for HIPAA we need a BAA. what's in scope? is model training in scope? we won't send PHI to model training, but inference logs could contain phi if misconfigured.
[10:20] Leah: BAAs cover our processing as a service; we don't use customer data to train models unless explicitly contracted. inference logs can be covered under the BAA and we offer options to restrict logs and provide encryption at rest and in transit.

[10:55] Tom: hypotheticals — if we pick Hosted in eu-west1 but later want to restrict keys, how painful is migrating to Dedicated or Private?
[11:08] Marco: we have migration paths — usually export of config and data and recreation in dedicated pools; timeline depends on data volume but we've done migrations in 2–6 weeks for pilot-scale. will capture steps in runbook.

[11:40] Jennifer: can you provide evidentiary audit logs for who accessed a particular request and what the output was? regulators ask for chain of custody.
[11:52] Marco: yes, we have request-level audit logs with request id, user id, model variant, timestamps, and optional output snapshot (if retention enabled). for Private you can ship logs to your SIEM for immutable storage.

[12:20] Aaron: about encryption, we require customer-managed KMS for keys. is there HSM support?
[12:30] Leah: yes, customer-managed keys backed by cloud KMS or HSM for Private and Dedicated; we can integrate with your enterprise HSM if needed.

[12:58] Sonia: anything about data residency for embeddings? we do embedding search for consumer features and don't want vectors leaving eu.
[13:08] Marco: embeddings are treated like any output — residency enforced by deployment. for hosted we can host model-serving in eu and ensure vector store resides in eu, but you need to control persistent vector DB. Private gives you full control of the vector store.

[13:45] Leah: competitor question — are you evaluating anyone else?
[13:50] Tom: yep openai for hosted simplicity, and vertex ai for deep cloud integration.

[14:05] Leah: good to know. where are you in procurement timeline?
[14:10] Aaron: pilot decision in 4–6 weeks, production by q4 if pilot successful. budget is allocated for pilot.

[14:30] Marco: potential configuration for pilot: Dedicated in eu region with CMK and logs forwarded to your SIEM, 2 gpus reserved, limited retention of outputs (30 days) with hashed pointers for long-term audit.

[15:02] Sonia: that sounds reasonable — we will need to validate latency. can we run a bench?
[15:08] Marco: yes, we can run benchmark tests — we usually do a 1–2 day perf run and share p50/p95/p99. will need sample payloads and expected concurrency.

[15:30] Jennifer: one more — are there any legal hold / e-discovery features? we sometimes are required to put holds on certain accounts.
[15:40] Leah: we support export of archives per account and can place holds on retention policies to prevent deletion. for Private you can fully control preservation.

[16:10] Tom: can you share an example of your RBAC and admin roles? audit trail for who changed policies is important.
[16:18] Priya: we have role-based access controls with admin, ops, read-only, etc., and an audit trail with who changed config and when. we can map to SSO groups.

[16:45] Aaron: what about PII detection? do you have automatic scrubbing?
[16:50] Marco: we provide configurable redaction pipelines and can integrate with your DLP. out-of-the-box there is a PII detector that can mask or remove tokens before storage.

[17:25] Sonia: in terms of data residency proof, will you provide documentation that the data never left eu?
[17:33] Leah: yes — we can provide an architecture attestation and logs showing data ingress/egress and region-specific endpoints. for Dedicated/Private we can provide stronger contractual guarantees.

[18:05] Aaron: ok cost question — what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated for pilot scale?
[18:12] Leah: quick ballpark: Hosted is usage-based, likely lower up-front, Dedicated has a modest monthly commit for reserved gpu capacity; i'll include numbers in the pricing sheet. for pilot the cost difference is often acceptable given the control Dedicated provides.

[18:45] Sonia: one more technical detail: model variants — if you fallback to a smaller model to reduce latency/cost, where does that happen and how are outputs logged?
[18:58] Marco: smart routing/fallback happens at the serving layer; we can log which variant served the request. fallback policy is configurable per route and will be included in the audit logs.

[19:28] Jennifer: any notable limitations for on-prem? network egress, support windows, or patching constraints?
[19:38] Marco: on-prem requires coordination for patching windows; we offer managed on-prem with a support SLA. network egress is in your control; we keep a control plane connection by default for telemetry but can run fully air-gapped on request.

[20:05] Leah: sounds like action items are to share SOC2/HIPAA docs, topology, pricing, and run the perf tests. any other asks?
[20:15] Aaron: please include sample terraform or IaC for dedicated/private setup.
[20:20] Marco: will do.

[20:45] Sonia: please also include recommended redaction patterns for card numbers and ssn-like tokens.
[20:50] Priya: will include templates.

[21:10] Leah: recap and next steps: leah send security packet and pricing; marco send topology and perf test plan; customer share pilot payloads and list of eu workloads. schedule technical deep dive next week.

[21:40] Jennifer: thanks everyone.
[21:42] Tom: thanks.
[21:43] Leah: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites.

[22:00] End of recording.

Notes: transcription has minor speaker overlap and some auto-caption errors; timestamps approximate. Links shared during call: security-deck.pdf (link), dedicated-pricing.xlsx (link), topology-diagram.png (link).
questions: Can Hosted guarantee no cross-border transfers if hosted in eu?
Do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM for Hosted or only Dedicated/Private?
How are audit logs preserved and can they be exported to customer SIEM?
What is migration path and timeline from Hosted -> Dedicated/Private?
Can you run perf benchmarks with our payloads and expected concurrency?
